sentence_stem: My hair was too long, so I
correct_completion: had it cut at the salon.
full_sentence: My hair was too long, so I had it cut at the salon.
acceptable_variants: got it cut by a hairdresser.

options.why_wrong: This shows the speaker doing the action personally. The causative 'have something done' needs 'had it cut' to show that someone else did the job.

options.text: had it cut at the salon.

options.why_wrong: 'Will' cannot be used with the past marker 'yesterday' in the same clause.

options.text: I had cut it by the salon.
options.why_wrong: Ungrammatical: 'by the salon' cannot follow a past-tense active verb here. Use 'had it cut at the salon' for the causative meaning.

grammar_focus: Causative 'have something done' (have + object + past participle)
explanation: The causative 'have something done' shows that the subject arranges for someone else to perform the action. The pattern is have + object + past participle, so 'had it cut' is correct. Portuguese speakers often use an active verb with 'I' as the subject here, because the first language usually expresses this idea with a different structure.
translation: Meu cabelo estava comprido demais, então eu o mandei cortar no salão.
